newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul high court upholds sentence for N.Korean spy.
newsitem.headline: Seoul high court upholds sentence for N.Korean spy.

text.p: A South Korean high court on Thursday upheld a 15-year sentence for a North Korean spy who posed as a Filipino university professor in Seoul, media reports said.
Chung Su-il, 62, lied about his name, age and nationality for more than a decade after arriving in South Korea in 1984 using forged documents.

Media reports quoted court statements as saying although Chung had caused serious harm to South Korean national security, he was entitled to a lenient sentence because he had converted from communism while living in the South.
The prosecution had originally demanded a death sentence for Chung.
Under the alias Mohamad Ali Kanso, Chung taught history at Dankook University from 1990.

He kept his identity secret from his South Korean wife of eight years. She thought he was 11 years younger than he really was, and had no idea he was already married with three daughters in North Korea.

He was arrested in a Seoul hotel last July while faxing information to a Pyongyang agent in Beijing on the deployment of recently imported Apache helicopters and the test firing of self-propelled artillery.
In reality, Chung worked for the external information research department of North Korea's ruling Worker's Party, and before beginning his spy career in Seoul, earned a master's degree in Lebanon.
The former professor of foreign studies at Pyongyang University gained Filipino nationality with fake papers.
South Korea has been technically at war with North Korea since the 1950-53 conflict which ended with a truce rather than a peace agreement.
